hints.title: Right To Left Column Addition
hints.text: Adding large numerical strings without standard big-integer conversion mirrors elementary grade-school addition from right to left with a carry digit.

hints.title: Simultaneous Traversal With Carry
hints.text: Process digits starting from the lowest significant place value, maintaining an integer carry between zero and one for each step.

hints.title: Digit Extraction And Reversal Procedure
hints.text: Use two pointers starting at the ends of both strings along with a carry variable. In each iteration, add the digits at the pointers if within bounds along with the carry. Append the sum modulo ten to the result and divide by ten for the next carry. Reverse the result at the end.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def addStrings(self, num1: str, num2: str) -> str:
        res = []
        i, j, carry = len(num1) - 1, len(num2) - 1, 0
        while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry:
            n1 = ord(num1[i]) - ord('0') if i >= 0 else 0
            n2 = ord(num2[j]) - ord('0') if j >= 0 else 0
            total = n1 + n2 + carry
            res.append(str(total % 10))
            carry = total // 10
            i -= 1
            j -= 1
        return "".join(reversed(res))
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(max(N, M)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting the input strings directly to built-in integers triggers integer overflow in languages with fixed integer widths and violates the explicit problem constraint.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Simulating digit addition processes each character in O(max(N, M)) time using only O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output string.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate must strictly avoid integer conversion libraries, handle strings of unequal length, and remember any trailing carry.
